title: Define each wagon as one separable, coherent, artifact-bounded unit of a journey

facts.note: Planner task text names wagons/trains/journeys or asks for domain decomposition.
Needs an observer that classifies a planning artifact as a wagon or train definition; no portable path glob is given by the source.
A wagon or train artifact is being authored or reshaped.
Planner phase must be reported by the harness.

fires: Planner adds a new wagon to a journey or train.
Planner splits one wagon into two or merges sibling wagons.
Planner rewrites a wagon's subject/action/goal, its measurable outcome, or its consumed/produced artifacts.
Planner adds, removes or moves features under a wagon, changing how the wagon's behavior is decomposed into features.
doesNotFire: Coder or tester work on how a wagon executes at runtime (code, handlers, tests).

Editing the wording or acceptances of a feature inside a wagon when the wagon's identity, artifacts, boundary, feature grouping, behavioral decomposition, subject/action/goal alignment and outcome measurability are all unaffected.
Planning documents that do not define or compose wagons.

given: A planner authors or reshapes a wagon in a journey, or composes wagons into a train.
when: The planner names the wagon and sets its boundary, artifacts and features.
then: Define the wagon as one subject/action/goal unit of the domain, separable from its siblings, that consumes and produces declared artifacts, groups the features decomposing its behavior, and composes into trains without a produce/consume cycle.
prefer: Cut the wagon from siblings along a correct boundary, judged by cross-wagon coupling.
Align subject, action and goal so the outcome is measurable.
Consume and produce declared artifacts across contracts.
Group under the wagon the features that decompose its behavior.
avoid: Wagons forming a produce/consume cycle with siblings in a train.
Describing how the wagon executes at runtime; that is a coder/tester concern.
Treating this definition as itself enforced; enforcement lives in the constraint/rule nodes that require it.
why: A wagon is the planner's domain-decomposition unit; a stable shared meaning lets the enforceable wagon conventions agree on what they protect.
evidence: This node is an advisory semantic anchor: it enforces nothing directly and is not bound to a validator; compliance is established transitively via planner.wagon.separability, planner.wagon.coupling-complexity, planner.wagon.semantic-coherence, planner.wagon.produce-consume-artifacts, planner.wagon.artifact-contracts, planner.wagon.no-consume-cycle and planner.wagon.features.

Reviewer confirms the wagon names one subject/action/goal with a measurable outcome, lists declared consumed/produced artifacts, groups the features decomposing its behavior, and does not close a produce/consume cycle in its train.
verifier_detail: Definition: wagon -> {separable, semantically-coherent, artifact-producing, artifact-consuming, acyclic, feature-bearing}.
separable: cut from siblings along a correct boundary (see planner.wagon.separability, planner.wagon.coupling-complexity).
semantically-coherent: subject/action/goal align, outcome is measurable (see planner.wagon.semantic-coherence).
artifacts: consumes and produces declared artifacts across contracts (see planner.wagon.produce-consume-artifacts, planner.wagon.artifact-contracts).
acyclic: wagons must not form a produce/consume cycle (see planner.wagon.no-consume-cycle).
feature-bearing: groups the features that decompose its behavior (see planner.wagon.features).

No direct detector: semantic_anchor = a definitional node that gives the artifact a stable meaning but is not itself bound to a validator; it is transitively protected by the enforceable constraint/rule nodes that require it.
audit: source kind: family (rewritten as kind rule for this schema)
source name: Wagon — advisory semantic anchor

splitSuggestion.then: Cut each wagon from its siblings along a correct boundary (judged with planner.wagon.coupling-complexity).
